title: Dashboard Lattice — Sprint Check-in & Cost Lab
content:
Sprint check-in notes from the observability 'Dashboard Lattice' workstream and accompanying cost-lab experiments. Focus this week: rework of dashboard data model, iteration on trace-sampling heuristic, and an initial cost alert prototype for high-span fanout flows.

Attendees: Priya Menon (owner), Liam Chen, Anya Vasilev, Marcus Holt, guest: SRE lead (Kelsey Park) for rollout coordination.

Meeting goals:
- Quick status across three tracks: dashboards, tracing sampling, cost telemetry alerts.
- Review preliminary numbers from the sampler A/B run.
- Align on dashboard ownership model and handoff steps to console team.
- Define next sprint's action items and PR checklist.

1) Dashboards: lattice model changes
- Summary: migrating several legacy heatmap widgets to the new 'lattice' data model to support per-route rollups and percentile bucketing. This reduces query fanout by consolidating tags and pre-aggregating top-10 dimensions in the pipeline.
- Work completed this sprint:
  - Prototype lattice index implemented in the telemetry pipeline (Liam).
  - Demo: 90s reduced cold-load for the main SLO dashboard when expanding timeframe from 1h -> 24h.
- Open questions:
  - Retention tradeoff: do we keep full coarse-grain lattice for 90d or drop to 30d? Cost delta rough estimate: 14% storage increase for 90d (Anya's calc).
  - Widget fallback behavior for low-cardinality routes (Marcus): If a route has <500 unique dimensions, show detailed dimensions instead of lattice rollup.
- Risks / mitigations:
  - Risk: mismatched derivations between console's percentiles and lattice pre-agg leading to small discrepancies. Mitigation: add a reconcile job (nightly diff) and surfaced mismatch alert (OBS-8421).

2) Tracing / sampling experiment recap (cost-lab A/B run):
- Experiment design: compare baseline uniform sampling at 20% vs adaptive sampler that reduces spans for long-tail microservices while preserving high-fanout traces at 60%.
- Deployment: ran for 7 full days on production traffic (weekend included) scoped to canary namespace.
- Key results:
  - Overall span volume reduction: 37% (adaptive) vs baseline.
  - Cost impact: estimated 19% lower storage and ingestion cost for tracing pipeline over the measured window.
  - Signal retention: alerts triggered on user-facing SLO regressions were unchanged (no missed alerts) in our sampled set.
  - Notable regressions: two internal-only legacy services saw trace reconstruction gaps (replay/forensics harder).
- Decisions:
  - Move forward with adaptive sampler but create explicit 'forensics' tag that forces 100% sampling for services flagged in a whitelist.
  - Add a 'retro-dump' feature to temporarily retain full traces for 48h on demand for debugging (Kelsey to spec).
- Action items from sampling track:
  - PR to relax sampler thresholds and add whitelist: GITHUB:pr/relax-sampler-117 (Liam) — target merge by 2027-11-28.
  - Run another 72h focused test including traffic from the two legacy services (Anya) — scheduled 2027-11-30.

3) Cost telemetry alerts and budget guardrails
- Prototype alert: 'span-fanout rise' — triggers when 1) a route's 5m span count jumps >4x baseline and 2) 95th pct tokenized span size increases >30%.
- Rationale: protect against sudden traffic patterns that spike ingestion and downstream billing (observed in a recent customer incident).
- Prototype metrics/thresholds validated on August–October historical data. False positives: about 2/day on low-traffic dev clusters.
- Proposal: apply alert to prod-only, with a 10m cooldown and an automated throttle suggestion in the ticketing payload.
- Next steps: implement automated 'throttle suggestion' that populates a ticket with rate-limiting steps and suggested sampling policy changes (Marcus).

4) Handoff & ownership to Console team
- Need: explicit ownership sheet that maps panels -> metric producer -> canonical query. This prevents drift from future console edits.
- Draft asset: CONFLUENCE:OBS-DASHBOARD-LATTICE (linked) contains the mapping and sample queries.
- Handoff plan:
  - Week +1: final schema freeze (Nov 30).
  - Week +2: Console team migration window (Dec 7–9).
  - Post-migration: 2-week oncall support from observability for lookups and reconciles.

5) Retro snippets (what went well / what to improve)
- Wins:
  - Faster iteration on dashboards thanks to pre-aggregates (reduced iteration time when adding widgets).
  - Sampling prototype produced measurable cost savings without surface-level alert loss.
- Improvements:
  - Need a better cross-team benchmark for 'forensics readiness' — currently ad-hoc. Suggest adding a small audit checklist for services that must retain full traces.
  - Documentation gaps: runbook steps for disabling adaptive sampling during incident are scattered. Action: consolidate into a single 'incidence playback' doc.

6) Blockers / escalations
- Blocker: KMS key rotations scheduled by infra overlap with our retention migration window (possible re-ingest failures if keys rotate mid-migration). Escalation: Priya to sync with infra security to push rotation to Dec 5 or add migration-safe fallback.
- Blocker: Console team capacity may push migration beyond Dec 9. Mitigation: identify minimal subset of panels (top 6) for Phase 1 and migrate them first.

7) Action items (owner + due date)
- Liam: finalize lattice index PR and add reconcile job stub (GH PR link in artifacts) — due 2027-11-28.
- Anya: run focused 72h sampler test including legacy services; report results — due 2027-12-01.
- Marcus: implement throttle-suggestion prototype for cost alerts and wire to ticket template — due 2027-12-05.
- Kelsey: spec retro-dump feature and runbook for temporary full-trace retention — due 2027-12-03.
- Priya: coordinate KMS rotation date with infra and confirm migration window — due 2027-11-25.

Notes / quick links:
- OBS-8421: reconcile job to surface lattice/console percentile mismatches (Jira).
- Gist: lattice schema example attached in Confluence page.
- Slack: see #obs-ops thread with the test dashboards and heatmap comparisons.

Misc scratch notes (notes to self):
- Consider adding a sampled-span pointer in lattice rows so we can rehydrate a representative trace for top-k routes. Could be used by the retro-dump flow to pick candidates.
- Low priority: evaluate cheaper cold storage for 90d lattice retention (Glacier-style) — estimate cost savings vs query latency.

Meeting adjourned at 14:25. Next check-in: weekly sync on 2027-11-30 14:00.

Document status: working draft — will be finalized after action items update.
